combo_label: The Pub × Silly English Things × Jane Austen

entries.clue: Sandwiches eaten in a stiff gale because the sun briefly came out
Highbury family in trade whose dinner party proves too tempting to refuse
Upturned bottle fitting that measures a single shot of spirit
Worldly brother and sister from town who upset a quiet country household
Sir Thomas's surname, carried by two sons and two ill-married daughters
Legal chain keeping land in the male line, dooming a houseful of girls
Ordinary fellow, in the plainest British word for a man in the street
Hooded waterproof, or the obsessive enthusiast wearing it
Recessed seat tucked beside an old fireplace, warm and sooty
Past all further use, of a tired body or a dying washing machine
Cue game played on a small coin-fed table in the corner of the bar
